title: Cold rebuild: fix "connection refused"
summary: Connect an API container to its database on a real Docker Engine, from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a skill stuck. In *app to database* you fixed an API that could not reach its database, on a real
Docker Engine. Now do it again from memory: the same scenario, **no hints, no solution to peek at**. The checks are
exactly the ones you passed the first time.
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old commands feels like knowing
them; doing it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: The API container starts at the same moment as Postgres and crashes with `Connection refused` to `db:5432`; a restart a few seconds later works. What is going on?
options: Postgres was still initialising and not accepting connections yet; the app needs to wait or retry
The DNS name `db` only becomes valid after a restart
Port 5432 must be published for the API to connect
The volume was locked by the first container
steps.explain: "Container started" is not "service ready". Retry with back-off in the app, and in Compose use a healthcheck with `depends_on: condition: service_healthy`.

steps.title: Fix "connection refused", cold
prompt: A real Docker Engine runs in this terminal. The database `db` (PostgreSQL-like, port 5432) is on the network `shop`,
and the API `api` (image `shop/api:3.0`, configured by `DB_HOST` and `DB_PORT`) cannot reach it.
Run a fixed `api` (same name, same image) so that its newest log line says `connected to ...:5432`.
From memory: no hints this time.
